figures.caption: Table 1. Performance comparison on the VinDR dataset. ViT-A and ViT-B correspond to DINOv2 [1] with a linear layer at input resolutions of 448×448 and 1024×1024 respectively. ViT-C demonstrates scores using a DeIT head instead of a linear layer at 448×448 input resolution.

Fig. 1. Overview. In our proposed method, we first use G-DINO in a zero-shot setting to localize semantically important Regions of Interest (RoIs) based on a clinically meaningful text prompt. The top-k RoIs, selected by bounding box confidence scores, are cropped and passed through a pretrained DINOv2 encoder to extract k feature vectors. These features are processed by a transformer module, enabling interaction among regions through self-attention. The global RoI (covering the full breast) is used as the final representation which is contextually enriched by fine-grained lesion-level RoIs, and is fed into a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) for classification.
